subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 27-year-old woman presents with dysuria, fever, and flank pain. Urine culture grows more than 100,000 CFU/mL of Escherichia coli. She is treated with oral ciprofloxacin and improves over the next 48 hours without complications.
question: Which of the following is the molecular target of this antibiotic?

options.text: Bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV

explanation_correct: Fluoroquinolones such as ciprofloxacin inhibit prokaryotic topoisomerase II (DNA gyrase) and topoisomerase IV, blocking DNA replication and causing double-stranded DNA breaks. These enzymes are bacterial, which provides selectivity over human topoisomerases.

explanation_incorrect.A: DNA polymerase III is not the target of fluoroquinolones; it is the main replicative polymerase in prokaryotes.
explanation_incorrect.C: The 30S ribosomal subunit is targeted by aminoglycosides and tetracyclines.
explanation_incorrect.D: Bacterial RNA polymerase is inhibited by rifampin.
explanation_incorrect.E: Dihydrofolate reductase is inhibited by trimethoprim, a folate synthesis antagonist.

educationalObjective: Fluoroquinolones inhibit bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV.
